cards.back: Unauthorized modification of a model's behavior or parameters.
Training data poisoning: the model learns deceptive behavior. Acts upstream.
Adversarial inputs crafted to bypass detection at inference time. Acts downstream.
Hostile instruction hidden in processed content that hijacks the original prompt.
Bypassing the model's safety guardrails to obtain prohibited content.
Fluent response that is factually false or fabricated.
Systematic bias in data or model producing discriminatory outcomes.
Ability to justify why the model produced a given output.
Confidential data disclosed, retained, or leaked through the AI system.
Personal data collected or processed without legal basis or control.
Fairness, transparency, accountability, and societal impact of AI systems.
Stealing or reusing a user's or AI agent's session to act with their privileges.
A tool-enabled agent tricked into executing unauthorized code or commands.
Injection = hostile content; jailbreaking = bypassing model rules.
Treat an AI agent like a privileged account: least privilege, logs, guardrails, reversibility.
Textbooks discuss AI as a defensive tool (EDR, UEBA), never as a threat vector. Source: exam objective §2.6.
13 official concepts: manipulation, poisoning, prompt injection, data loss, bias, explainability, hallucinations, jailbreaking, evasion, privacy, ethics, session hijacking, code execution.
